reason: Every consumer only needs to be told that a file or one directory level may have changed and then re-reads it; one harness watch service gives that over operating-system notifications with a stat-polling fallback, and the only recursive watch (in-process code reload) is not carried over.

The grep, glob and file-name searches run in process in pure Go behind a Searcher interface, so the release carries no second executable and search uses the same filesystem view and sandbox policy as file reads; the regular-expression dialect becomes Go's.

Line diffs with three context lines are computed on the host by one package over go-udiff with a deterministic size bound; the browser-side diff disappears because the host renders the UI, and Git patch text is not parsed at all, because the code-host UI shows status only (DH-ADR-38).

The library supplies one scoring function inside upstream's own 300-line search module; the Go port keeps the tiers and folding rules and replaces the call with a scorer written for the word-start rule, using golang.org/x/text for Unicode normalisation.

The library's only use is the text search of the plugin market index. The owner decided that plugins are installed from local directories and that the harness downloads and discovers none (DH-ADR-13), and the boot area records that the plugin market is not built (DH-ADR-BOOT-11), so there is nothing to search and no index is built.

Streaming a session export as a ZIP and reading an uploaded ZIP with per-entry limits are both covered by the standard library's archive/zip, whose pull-based reader also removes three limits upstream documents for chat import.
It exists only for upstream's build process: its three call sites unpack the downloaded Node runtime, a Python wheel and the Electron runtime while packaging, and the Go release bundles none of them.

Reading a gzip tarball from the network with strict path, type, duplicate and size checks, and writing reproducible tarballs, are done with the standard library's archive/tar and compress/gzip plus the harness's own entry checks.

Bounded fan-out is an errgroup with SetLimit; the two session-store limiters disappear because listing becomes a database query, and the GitLab pool keeps the idiom with cancellation on first failure.

Ordinary file work maps onto the Go standard library; the operations where Go and Node differ or upstream has several implementations (atomic replacement, create-if-absent, locks, file identity, containment, owner-only creation) are owned by one harness package that uses golang.org/x/sys for the missing system calls.

Path building maps onto path/filepath for disk paths and path for forward-slash paths, with conversion at the boundary; containment tests done upstream by string comparison go through one function or a directory-rooted handle.

Home and temporary directories, platform, processor count and host name come from the os and runtime packages; operating-system version and memory, used only for diagnostics, come from golang.org/x/sys in build-tagged files.

gzip and DEFLATE come from the standard library; Zstandard, which Go 1.27.4 does not offer as a public package, is no longer the live session format and remains only as an optional stored-payload codec through klauspost/compress, while exports use gzip.

title: No shared file-watch service: five private watchers, the same close-time error workaround copied into three packages, and two major versions of the watcher library installed side by side

reason: One watch service owns the watcher and defines one close contract (close returns only after the callback can no longer run, late errors are discarded inside the service), so consumers carry no workaround and one module version is used.

title: The ripgrep executable is located by three packaging-specific code paths, and each packaging (desktop archive, macOS signing, Python runtime, browser worker) needs its own step to carry, unpack, sign or stub it

reason: Search is Go code inside the one release binary, so there is no executable to find, unpack, sign or stub in any packaging.

title: Diff work is bounded inconsistently: wall-clock time on the host (so the recorded hunks depend on machine load), an edit-distance cap in the browser, and no bound for tool-result diffs

reason: All diffs are computed by one host package whose bound depends only on the size of the two texts, so the same inputs always give the same stored result.

title: The fuzzy-match library does not fit the word-start rule it is used for: each word start is prepared and tried as a separate target, and the library's process-lifetime cache has to be avoided by the caller

reason: The Go scorer searches word-start alignments directly and keeps no global state, so neither workaround is needed.

title: Atomic file replacement is implemented three times with three different durability guarantees, two of them calling Windows system functions through a foreign-function library that must be built or downloaded

reason: One harness helper replaces files with an explicit durability argument on every platform, and its Windows calls go through golang.org/x/sys without a foreign-function bridge.
